deep.reconstruction:
PROBLEM. Gauss analyses a 'Baumann comet seeker' with an achromatic objective (focal length 862, aperture 52, thickness 15) and a three-lens eyepiece (focal lengths 181.8, 97.3, 67.3; diameters 60.8, 45.4, 38; thicknesses 6.5, 5.4, 5.0). All lenses are treated as thin. The separations are d0 = 772.7 (objective to lens 1), d1 = 94.2 (lens 1 to lens 2) and d2 = 14.2 (lens 2 to lens 3). The units are evidently mm. The numbers 5576, 2984, 2065 are the same three focal lengths in another unit; each ratio is about 30.67. The previous page sets up a third-order spherical-aberration sum for 4 thin lenses, using the same symbols α, β.

(1) PARAXIAL RAY TRACE (Gauss's continued-fraction / Dioptrische Untersuchungen scheme). The tables are reproduced by the alternating-sign recursion below [the recursion is my reconstruction; every value checks].
- Rule: a_{k+1} = d_k*b_k - a_k and b_{k+1} = a_{k+1}/f_{k+1} - b_k.
- Chain A is the axial (marginal) ray. It starts with α = 1 and β = 1/862 = 0.00116009.
  - α' = 772.7β - 1 = -0.103596, and β' = α'/181.8 - β = -0.00172993.
  - α'' = 94.2β' - α' = -0.059363, and β'' = α''/97.3 - β' = +0.00111983.
  - α''' = 14.2β'' - α'' = +0.075265, and β''' = α'''/67.3 - β'' = -0.00000146.
  - So β''' ≈ 0 and the system is almost afocal.
- Chain C is the chief ray: unit angle through the objective centre. It starts with γ = 0 and δ = 1.
  - γ' = 772.70, and δ' = γ'/181.8 - δ = 4.2503 - 1 = 3.2503.
  - γ'' = 94.2δ' - γ' = -466.52, and δ'' = γ''/97.3 - δ' = -4.7947 - 3.2503 = -8.0450.
  - Gauss writes γ''' = 14.2δ'' - γ'' = +342.28. The correct value is +352.28.
  - δ''' = γ'''/67.3 - δ'' = 5.0859 + 8.0450 = 13.1309, which is consistent with his 342.28.
- The invariant αδ - βγ = 1 should hold after every lens. It shows the slip: with Gauss's numbers α'''δ''' - β'''γ''' = 0.9888, whereas with 352.28 it is 1.0000.
- The angular magnification is about δ''' ≈ 1/α'''. The correct value is ≈ 13.28; Gauss's value is 13.13.

(2) 'WEGEN HELLIGKEIT' — the unvignetted field. The axial pencil diameter at lens k is 52|α_k|: 5.4, 3.1 and 3.9. The free margin is the lens diameter minus this:
- 60.8 - 5.4 = 55.4;
- 45.4 - 3.1 = 42.3;
- 38 - 3.9 = 34.1.
The chief-ray height per radian is |γ_k|, so the full field angle allowed by lens k is margin/|γ_k| radians:
- 55.4/772.7 → 246';
- 42.3/466.52 → 312';
- 34.1/342.28 → 342'.
The fully illuminated field is therefore limited by lens 1 to about 246', i.e. about 4.1°.

(3) MYOPIC EYE with far point t = 147 mm. The writing is f = 1/862 and K = δ'''^2·t·f. The exact equation is 1/(fx) = K(1 - fx), i.e. 1/(fx(1 - fx)) = K. Expanding gives 1/(fx) = K - 1 - fx - ...
- K = 13.1309^2·147/862 = 29.40, so the first approximation is 1/(fx) ≈ 28.4 ('Hier = 28,4').
- Hence x = 862/28.4 ≈ 30.4 mm. This is the change in the objective–eyepiece separation needed for focusing.
- To first order x ≈ f_obj^2/(M^2 t), the standard refocusing formula.
- The exact provenance of the (1 - fx) factor is not shown on the page.

(4) 'FARBIGER RAND' — lateral colour at the field edge. The sum is Σ_k α_k·(γ_k/f_k) over the eyepiece lenses:
- 4.2503·(-0.103596) = -0.440;
- -4.7947·(-0.059363) = +0.285;
- 5.0859·(0.075266) = +0.382.
The sum is +0.227. Multiplied by 7500" (≈125', the half-field from (2)) this gives about 1703"; Gauss writes 1707"5. Dividing by about 48 (an assumed dispersion number of the glass) gives about 35.5"; Gauss writes 35"6. This is the colour fringe at the field edge. The sum is the thin-lens transverse-colour coefficient Σ y·ȳ·φ/ν.
errors: γ''' = 14.2·δ'' - γ'' = -114.24 + 466.52 = 352.28, not 342.28 as written. Everything downstream inherits the 10-unit slip: δ''' (13.13 instead of ≈13.28); the third field limit (342' instead of ≈333'); the coloured-rim term (5.086 instead of 5.234, sum 0.227 instead of ≈0.238); and the myopic refocus (x ≈ 30.4 instead of ≈29.7). The slip is detectable through the invariant α'''δ''' - β'''γ''' = 1, which with his figures comes out 0.9888.
0.227 × 7500 = 1702.5, not 1707.5 as written (assuming the reading is right). The final 35"6 follows from 1707.5/48; the correct figure is ≈35.5.
α''' = 0.0752646, written 0.075266. This is a negligible rounding difference.

results.what: Paraxial thin-lens ray trace through a 4-lens telescope by alternating-sign recursion, using two fundamental solutions (axial ray and chief ray) with unit determinant
results.modern_name: y-nu paraxial ray trace / ray-transfer (ABCD) matrices; Gaussian constants of a lens system
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841); matrix form later (Sampson 1913, etc.)

results.what: Unvignetted field of view from free lens margins divided by chief-ray heights
results.modern_name: vignetting / field stop analysis with marginal and chief rays
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-19th c. telescope design practice (Euler, Klügel)

results.what: Refocusing displacement of the eyepiece for a myopic eye, x ≈ f_obj^2/(M^2 t) with a second-order correction
Lateral colour as the sum Σ (marginal height)·(chief height)·(power), times field angle and dispersion
results.modern_name: transverse (lateral) chromatic aberration coefficient Σ y ȳ φ/ν
results.usually_credited_to: Eyepiece achromatism conditions: Euler, Boscovich, Klügel (18th c.); systematic form by Seidel-era authors

deep.surprise_reason: This is a competent design check of a real comet seeker using Gauss's own paraxial recursion, plus standard field, refocusing and lateral-colour estimates. The lateral-colour sum in y·ȳ·φ form is a nice explicit instance, but eyepiece achromatism conditions of this type were known from Euler, Boscovich and Klügel. Gauss's dioptric work is well documented.

checkable.asserts: the invariant α'''δ'''-β'''γ''' with Gauss's γ'''=342.28 gives ≈0.988 rather than 1, exposing the slip

transcription_corrections: In the myopia formula the product should read δ'''δ''' (i.e. δ'''^2), not δ''δ''': only 13.1309^2·147/862 - 1 = 28.4 reproduces 'Hier = 28,4'.
Under 1707"5 the mark read as '=4' is probably ':48', a divisor that gives 35"6.
The 'Wegen Helligkeit' entries 5,4 / 3,1 / 3,9 are pencil diameters 52|α_k|. The second column gives the free margins 55,4 / 42,3 / 34,1, and the third the field angles 246' / 312' / 342'.
The header 'Distanz von 3' is uncertain; the column gives the separations objective–1, 1–2 and 2–3 (772,7; 94,2; 14,2).
In the coloured-rim lines the first factor reads 4,2503 (= γ'/f'). The listed δ' = 3,2503 is 4,2503 - 1.
